WhatsApp is developing a new feature that lets users connect third-party AI agents to the app, chat with them, and issue commands for them to carry out tasks. Here are the details.

WhatsApp is developing support for third-party agents

When OpenClaw and similar platforms first took off, one of the primary ways users interacted with agents remotely was by connecting them to instant messaging apps.

However, many users soon discovered that setting up bots to converse with third-party AI agents on WhatsApp could result in their WhatsApp accounts being banned.

Meanwhile, Telegram rode that wave and has since become one of the main platforms for users to converse with or instruct agents, which can run locally on the user's computer or in the cloud.

Now, according to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is working on bringing native support for third-party AI agents to its users, allowing them to connect agents directly to dedicated chats within the app through a new feature.

Once a new bot is set up within WhatsApp, the app generates an API key that users can subsequently use to connect an agent to the chat. As WABetaInfo explains: "The exact steps depend on the platform, but most services have a field where you can paste" the API key, allowing users to start chatting with third-party agents right through WhatsApp.

Here's what WABetaInfo had to say:

The site notes that only some Android users currently have access to the new feature, but it is expected to roll out more widely in the near future. WABetaInfo says WhatsApp's implementation supports up to five agents per account and lets users customize a name and avatar for each one. However, conversations with third-party agents are not yet end-to-end encrypted.
